title: Implement Web Workers for PDF Processing
description: Offload CPU-intensive operations (PDF load, merge, assemble, split, stamp) from the main thread to Web Workers to ensure smooth UI responsiveness.

steps.details: Import PDFManager and set up self.onmessage event listener to handle MERGE, SPLIT, ASSEMBLE, and NUMBER operations.

steps.task: Refactor PDFManager to receive transferable ArrayBuffers
steps.details: Ensure methods can accept raw ArrayBuffers/Uint8Arrays instead of File objects directly if needed, or parse them on the worker thread.

steps.task: Create worker wrapper client / React hook
steps.details: Implement a custom hook to instantiate the worker, send jobs, transfer ArrayBuffers, handle cleanups, and manage progress states.
Replace direct static calls to PDFManager with the new worker hooks, updating loading indicators.

technicalNotes.bundlerCompatibility: Next.js 16 natively compiles Web Workers instantiated via: new Worker(new URL('./pdf.worker.ts', import.meta.url))
technicalNotes.transferableObjects: Transfer ArrayBuffer instances instead of copying them to avoid serialization overhead across threads.
